## Summary

Wires kill-me Azure OIDC jobs to explicit GitHub Actions environments using the cross-repo contract:

```yaml
environment: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && 'prod' || 'dev' }}
```

Commit `c1b6725` applies that wiring to:

- `.github/workflows/docker-build-check.yaml` job `build`
- `.github/workflows/build-and-deploy.yaml` job `build-and-deploy`
- `.github/workflows/snapshot.yaml` job `generate-and-commit`

## Feature Contracts

Affected contracts:

- [x] GitHub Actions Azure OIDC environment subject contract: main uses `prod`; non-main branches use `dev`.
- [x] ACR image build/publish workflow contract for `docker-build-check.yaml` and `build-and-deploy.yaml`.
- [x] Snapshot Azure App Configuration/Cosmos snapshot generation workflow contract.

Contract behavior:

- Main-branch Azure-auth jobs continue to use the `prod` GitHub environment, preserving the intended production OIDC subject shape.
- Non-main branch workflow runs use the `dev` GitHub environment, so branch `workflow_dispatch` and prebuild-style runs do not authenticate with plain branch-ref OIDC subjects.
- `tofu.yaml` was inspected but left unchanged because it delegates to a reusable workflow job rather than defining a local first-party `runs-on` job containing `azure/login`.

Evidence:

- `yq e '.'` over all `.github/workflows/*.{yaml,yml}` files: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- `npm run build` in `frontend`: passed, with existing Vite chunk/dynamic-import warnings.
- `npm run lint` in `frontend`: passed with 11 pre-existing React hook dependency warnings and 0 errors.
- PR CI on `c1b6725`: Docker Build Check passed; Lint passed.
- Branch `workflow_dispatch` for `docker-build-check.yaml` on `tank/session/1065/kill-me` with `git_ref=tank/session/1065/kill-me` passed: https://github.com/romaine-life/kill-me/actions/runs/27733231893. The dispatched run successfully completed Azure OIDC login, ACR login, ACR candidate lookup, and ACR import under the non-main branch environment wiring.
- Restricted-git publish initially failed because the default app token lacked workflow-file permission; the approved break-glass grant was used to publish `c1b6725` to `tank/session/1065/kill-me`.
